problem: A projectile is launched at 20 m/s at 30° above horizontal from ground level. Take g = 10 m/s². Find (a) the time of flight, (b) the maximum height reached, and (c) the horizontal range.

steps.prompt: Decompose the launch velocity into horizontal and vertical components.
reveal: u_x = u · cos θ = 20 × cos 30° = 17.32 m/s
u_y = u · sin θ = 20 × sin 30° = 10 m/s

steps.prompt: The horizontal motion has no acceleration. The vertical motion accelerates downward at g. Sketch the trajectory.
reveal: Horizontal: a_x = 0   →   u_x stays at 17.32 m/s.
Vertical:   a_y = −g  →   slows on the way up, speeds on the way down.

steps.prompt: At the highest point the vertical velocity is zero. Use v = u + a·t to find the time to reach the top.
By symmetry, the projectile takes the same time to come back down. So time of flight T = 2 · t_top.
Use v² = u² − 2·g·H at the highest point (where v = 0) to find the maximum height H.
The horizontal range is simply the horizontal speed times the total flight time. R = u_x · T.

finalAnswer: T = 2 s    H = 5 m    R ≈ 34.6 m
bonus: Shortcut formula:  R = u² · sin(2θ) / g  =  (20)² · sin 60° / 10  =  400 × 0.866 / 10  ≈  34.64 m
